Finn Gomez | Getty Images Meta has been assigned a negative outlook by S&P Global Ratings on concerns surrounding cash flow and AI spending. The credit agency said Friday that the outlook reflects "uncertainty" surrounding Meta's elevated capex and its negative free cash flow. Meta's credit rating has thus been reduced from AA- stable to AA- negative, the S&P Global Ratings said. S&Ps highest credit rating is AAA. Anything below BBB falls into the junk bond category. The social media giant said in its third-quarter earnings report last week that it expects full-year capex to come in the range of $135 billion to $145 billion. The company also posted negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion, going in the red for the first time. Investors sent Meta shares sinking 7% following last week's earnings report despite though the company beating on revenue. The stock finished October down 15%, its worst month in four years. The company said on Monday that it plans to raise $95 billion to help fund its AI initiatives, with plans to first raise $35 billion in underwritten public equity offerings, followed by an additional $60 billion to be raised via an at-the-market program. Meta didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. headlines.article_text: Amazon, Intel shares fall after earnings amid AI spending concerns Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Intel shares fell 29% on Friday, posting the stock's worst day since the 1970s. The chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected guidance, citing ongoing softness in the PC market. Amazon also sold off following an earnings miss. In this article AMZN INTC Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan speaks during a keynote presentation at Computex in Taipei on June 2, 2026. Cheng Yu-chen | Afp | Getty Images Intel shares plummeted 29% on Friday, their worst day since the 1970s, after the chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected guidance due to a plant shutdown in Israel and ongoing softness in the PC market. It's a major setback for CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who was hired in March 2025, and has since been on a campaign to revive the company after it missed out on the early years of the artificial intelligence boom. Intel's plunge is also a big hit to the Trump administration, which led the U.S. government into taking a 10% stake in the company over a year ago. While it's still a profitable investment, the value of those holdings dropped by about $12 billion on Friday. Nvidia also took a big stake in Intel, and its stock dropped by about $6 billion in value. Heading into Thursday's earnings report, Intel shares were up about 150% this year, buoyed by demand for central processors, which are becoming critical to agentic AI workloads. Analysts at D.A. Davidson downgraded the stock to neutral from buy on Friday in a report titled, "Not fixed yet." "We understand the PC market is being impacted at the industry level," the analysts wrote. "However it is hard to justify the current multiple when weakness is so significant." Amazon and Intel stock chart Amazon shares also sold off on Friday, slipping 1.4%, after the company reported a third-quarter miss on the top and bottom line while maintaining its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 of $220 billion. Amazon also reported negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter, and a big increase from the previous period. The Nasdaq Composite slid 2.9%, capping off a week of rough tech earnings. Alphabet on Thursday suffered its worst day on record, plunging more than 12%. The stock fell again on Friday. Other semiconductor names also notched declines. Chip giant Nvidia fell 4%, while Broadcom dropped more than 5% and mobile chipmaker Qualcomm tumbled 11%. Not a 'moment of reckoning' Investors are growing nervous about the massive AI spending from the tech giants and whether their investments will pay off. "I don't think this is a moment of reckoning but I think it's a moment where investors should take a long thought about how positioning across the space still remains crowded even though the fundamentals are strong," Matt Orton, chief market strategist at Raymond James, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Friday. For Intel, the disappointing forecast reflects a PC market that's getting hammered due to soaring costs for memory and other components. Global PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier, according to Counterpoint Research . Analysts were expecting revenue of $17.1 billion and EPS of 43 cents, according to LSEG. "We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," Intel finance chief David Zinsner, said in the release. "We will continue making disciplined investments in capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth." The guidance also accounts for the effects of an explosion at a fab in Israel that killed two workers and seriously injured a third earlier this month. The incident will cost the company about $600 million in lost revenue over two quarters, Zinsner said. Tan said the explosion, which he called an "unfortunate and tragic accident," caused an "extended shutdown" at the plant, impacting shipments of 10-nanometer chips. Key to Tan's turnaround effort is Intel's foundry business, which has struggled to find its footing. Intel is the only U.S.-based manufacturer of advanced logic chips, and is now in high-volume production of its most advanced 18A chip out of its new fab in Arizona, providing an alternative to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co . Its next Arizona fab is expected to begin operations by the end of 2028. Intel still has no external customers for its new chips. "We're going to have a couple of customers ready to announce the next two quarters," Tan said on the call, adding that Intel is making "tremendous progress" on its coming 14A chips. headlines.article_text: Reddit plunges 29% after issuing weak outlook for its worst day ever Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Reddit fell 29.22% on Friday, wrapping its worst day since the company went public in 2024. The social media company reported weak sales guidance in its third-quarter earnings report. Reddit also announced it will test requiring users to log in to use the platform as AI continues to hit search referral numbers. In this article RDDT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:00 01:00 Reddit shares fall double digits on lighter-than-expected daily active users Closing Bell: Overtime Shares of Reddit cratered 29.22% on Friday, the worst drop since becoming a public company in 2024, after the company forecast weak fourth-quarter sales in its latest earnings report . The previous record low was set on July 31, when the stock dropped 20.99%. The social media company on Thursday projected fourth-quarter sales between $1 billion and $1.03 billion, below analysts' estimates of $1.05 billion. Reddit reported Q3 sales growth of 53% over a year ago, weaker than previous quarters, but beat Wall Street expectations on both earnings and revenue. The report comes as the company has seen a shift in its search referral traffic with the rise of Google's AI Overview. In an interview with CNBC, Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said search-referral traffic from Google went "down meaningfully in this quarter" due to AI. Reddit announced on Thursday that it plans to test requiring users to log in to access content, a dramatic change from a site whose community-based discussion content has become synonymous with the open internet. Google's shift towards pushing AI overviews in search results coincided with the change, intended to help boost the number of logged-in users that are more active on the platform, which in turn helps the company's advertising business, according to Huffman. "Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me. I've been holding that line," Huffman said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work." Multiple analysts downgraded the stock following Reddit's disappointing results, with Citizens noting that "search changes highlight the problem with selling content to Google" and that as referral problems worsen, uncertainty around user growth amid the login requirement switch "puts more pressure on user monetization." — CNBC's Jonathan Vanian contributed to this report. headlines.article_text: Binance hack: Zhao asks Elon Musk to stop trolling Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Binance's cofounder Changpeng Zhao urged Elon Musk to stop mocking the exchange after it suffered a $6.3 billion hack. In this article SPCX TSLA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Changpeng Zhao, co-founder of Binance Holdings Ltd., during the Bitcoin Asia conference in Hong Kong, China, on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. Chan Long Hei | Bloomberg | Getty Images Changpeng Zhao, the cofounder and former CEO of Binance , asked Elon Musk not to "troll" the company on Friday and instead "show some support" after the SpaceX CEO appeared to mock the embattled cryptocurrency exchange in a series of social media posts. After learning the world's largest crypto exchange had been hit by a $6.3 billion hack late Thursday, Musk posted several emojis, ranging from laughing to grimacing, on X. In response, Zhao reminded the SpaceX and Tesla CEO of Binance's equity stake in Musk's businesses. Binance’s SpaceX stake, which stems from an earlier investment in what was then-Twitter, is worth more than $1 billion, Zhao said. That's a tiny fraction of SpaceX's roughly $2 trillion valuation. "Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop," Zhao wrote. "Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion. Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!" It's not the first time the pair has sparred online. In Nov. 2021, Binance suspended Dogecoin withdrawals because of a wallet glitch, a measure Musk called "shady". In reply, Zhao highlighted a major Tesla recall of almost 12,000 U.S. vehicles due to software glitches and hardware issues. Binance froze all withdrawals and deposits after the hack, which investigators suspect to be the work of North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit TraderTraitor. It has since restored deposits.
